stories.body: Former Bank of Spain governor Pablo Hernández de Cos is set to become the first Spaniard to lead the European Central Bank. France and Germany backed him in a deal that also gives ECB executive board seats to France’s Laurence Boone and Germany’s Markus Brunnermeier. The European Council is expected to formalize the appointments in December, ahead of Christine Lagarde’s departure in February. Eurozone inflation reached 4% in October, up from 2.1% a year earlier.
stories.headline: EU leaders back Pablo Hernández de Cos to lead the European Central Bank

stories.body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia was preparing a large-scale strike in the coming days and urged Ukrainians to heed missile alerts. A Russian ballistic missile attack wounded seven people in Kyiv overnight, the city’s mayor said. Zelensky told the BBC that delays in US deliveries of Patriot interceptors were costing lives and called for more pressure on Moscow before peace talks expected in December. US President Donald Trump said he had urged Vladimir Putin at their meeting in China to scale back Russia’s military aggression across Europe.
stories.headline: Zelensky warns of a major Russian strike and urges the US to press Moscow

stories.body: Two Italian Rheinmetall technicians who were supporting Kuwait’s air defenses died after a strike on a facility in Kuwait. Kuwaiti authorities said a Kuwaiti and a Pakistani national were also injured. Kuwait blamed Iran, and Italy’s foreign minister said investigators had identified the drone as Iranian-made. Tehran denied carrying out the strike and offered to help Kuwait and Italy investigate.
stories.headline: Two Italians killed in Kuwait strike that Iran denies carrying out

stories.body: Officials at Shifa and Al-Aqsa Martyrs hospitals said five Israeli strikes and a shooting killed 10 Palestinians across Gaza on Thursday and overnight. A strike on a residential apartment in Deir al-Balah, in central Gaza, killed a married couple.
stories.headline: Gaza hospitals report 10 Palestinians killed in Israeli attacks

stories.body: New Zealand’s final election count gave Prime Minister Christopher Luxon’s National Party and its two coalition partners 65 seats in the 130-seat parliament. Luxon is opening talks with the centrist Opportunity Party, which won seven seats. The Labour-led bloc would still fall short with Opportunity’s support. A recount that returns one seat to National could restore the coalition’s majority. If the count stands and talks fail, another election is possible.
stories.headline: New Zealand’s governing coalition falls one seat short of a majority

stories.body: The Office for National Statistics estimated that 738,000 people moved to the UK and 661,000 left in the year through June. Net migration was down 92% from its March 2023 peak of 944,000. Fewer people arrived from outside Europe for work or study, asylum claims fell, and emigration remained relatively high. Visa restrictions introduced by the previous Conservative government and continued under Labour contributed to the decline.
stories.headline: UK net migration falls to 77,000, its lowest since 1997 outside the pandemic

stories.body: Thanksgiving storms left nearly a million homes and businesses without power on Thursday evening, with outages concentrated in eastern states. More than 2,000 flights were delayed and over 400 were canceled, according to FlightAware. New York City’s Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade was postponed to Saturday. In Maryland, nearly two million people in Montgomery and Prince George’s counties were asked to conserve water after power disruptions affected two filtration plants.
stories.headline: Thanksgiving storms knock out power to nearly a million and disrupt Maryland water service

stories.body: People’s Party leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo made the pledge during Spain’s only four-way election debate before Sunday’s vote. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and Broad Front candidate Ada Colau challenged him over a possible coalition with Vox, whose leader Santiago Abascal declined to specifically condemn violence against women. Sánchez and Colau attacked Vox’s proposed spending cuts, while Feijóo and Abascal both backed lower taxes. On housing, Colau called for rents to fall 30%, while Sánchez pledged to build more homes.
stories.headline: Feijóo vows to step down if he fails to become prime minister

stories.body: Spain’s Supreme Court rejected the government’s argument that a temporary voting suspension applied only to citizens living abroad. The court said its order covers those on the government’s list who obtained citizenship under the grandchildren law, including 11,283 who live in Spain. It said 901 people who submitted consular certificates proving descent from Spanish exiles could vote.
stories.headline: Spain’s Supreme Court bars more than 163,000 new citizens from voting on Sunday

stories.body: The Med Emre was carrying up to 7,000 metric tons of diesel from Algeciras to Barcelona when it capsized about 46 kilometers off Ibiza. All 17 crew members were rescued, but one later died and six others received hospital treatment. Maritime authorities said a small surface slick had dissipated and a rescue ship had secured the partially submerged tanker. Divers and technicians were due to inspect the hull on Friday before authorities decided where to tow it.
stories.headline: Diesel tanker capsizes off Ibiza, killing one crew member

stories.body: High-speed train tickets between Barcelona and Madrid averaged €62.40 in the first half of November, down from an average of €86.80 for the full month of November last year, according to 3Cat’s price tracking. Ouigo had the lowest average fare at €42.80, followed by Iryo at €63.20 and Renfe at €67. 3Cat linked the lower fares to weaker demand after the Urda and Adamuz rail crashes on the line toward Seville.
stories.headline: Barcelona–Madrid high-speed rail fares fall 28% in 3Cat price tracking
